details: Importing `ukraine69` in versions 1.2.0 through 1.2.2 scans for local `.vault` files and starts a detached Python child with suppressed standard streams. When a vault contains usable `auth_key` and `api_id` fields, the child attempts Telegram `account.deleteAccount` through `goygram`, then attempts to delete the local vault and adjacent `.session` file even if the API call fails. A generated script also removes `ukraine69` files, distribution metadata, and cache traces after a delay. Version 1.2.2 broadens vault discovery and changes the GoyGram call path. Version 1.2.3 replaces the deletion path with import-triggered reconnaissance: a detached child scans for vaults, reads up to three vaults found in the user's home or working directory, and writes their first 200 bytes plus environment and filesystem observations to `/tmp/.u69_recon.log` and `~/.u69_recon.log`. This release has no observed network exfiltration or account-deletion call. All four releases advertise Ukrainian locale helpers; installation alone does not execute the module. Actual account deletion, later use of the local logs, and victim execution have not been established by this static analysis.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
